note: passez du bon temps is ongoing present; English 'have a good time' can read as a future wish.
proposed_target: J'espère que vous passez du bon temps !
proposed_english: I hope you're having a good time!

note: raconter de telles choses sur moi is more exactly 'tell such things about me' than generic 'say'.
proposed_target: Comment oses-tu raconter de telles choses sur moi !
proposed_english: How dare you tell such things about me!

note: French is an interrogative; English incorrectly uses exclamation punctuation.
proposed_target: Mais qu'as-tu donc fait pendant tout ce temps ?
proposed_english: What have you been doing all this time?

note: échec means failure; 'lack of success' unnecessarily weakens the meaning.
proposed_target: Es-tu en train de me reprocher ton échec ?
proposed_english: Are you blaming me for your failure?

note: déjeuner means have lunch, not have dinner.
proposed_english: Are you going to have lunch here with me?

note: For standard written French, negation requires ne: je n'ai aucun.
proposed_target: Es-tu en train de dire que je n'ai aucun sens de l'humour ?
proposed_english: Are you saying I have no sense of humor?

note: dépourvu de cerveau is stilted/unidiomatic for this basic conversational meaning; use natural French.
proposed_target: Veux-tu dire que je n'ai pas de cerveau ?
proposed_english: Are you saying that I don't have a brain?

note: Voulez-vous means 'Do you want'; ce travail is 'this work', while English says 'that work'.
proposed_english: Do you want to help me with this work?

note: offrir un verre means offer/buy someone a drink; the English 'wet your whistle' is unnecessary slang and poor learner alignment.
proposed_english: Can I buy you a drink?

note: The French question incorrectly ends with a period.
proposed_target: Puis-je avoir deux hamburgers et un coca, s'il vous plaît ?
proposed_english: Can I have two hamburgers and a Coke, please?

note: Pourriez-vous is conditional 'Could you', not 'Can you'.
proposed_target: Pourriez-vous repasser ce t-shirt pour moi, s'il vous plaît ?
proposed_english: Could you iron this T-shirt for me, please?

note: Pourriez-vous is conditional 'Could you', not 'Can you'.
proposed_target: Pourriez-vous me dire où se trouve le restaurant, s'il vous plaît ?
proposed_english: Could you please tell me where the restaurant is?

note: Accent required in plaît; répéter votre nom means repeat your name, not simply tell it once more.
proposed_target: Pouvez-vous s'il vous plaît me répéter votre nom ?
proposed_english: Can you please repeat your name?

note: English adds 'still', which is absent; Arrives-tu à te rappeler asks whether the person can manage to remember.
proposed_target: Arrives-tu à te rappeler le moment où nous nous sommes rencontrés pour la première fois ?
proposed_english: Can you remember the time we first met?
